|work=The Star |date=7 May 2026 |language=en}} ==Summary== ===Background=== Sheffield City Council was created in 1974 as a [[metropolitan borough]]. [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] saw early success, controlling the council from its creation until [[1999 Sheffield City Council election|1999]] when the [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] took control.{{cite web |title=BBC News - Election 2011 - England council elections - Sheffield |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/special/election2011/council/html/cg.stm |website=BBC News |access-date=12 January 2026}} This lasted until [[2002 Sheffield City Council election|2002]], when the council fell into [[no overall control]].{{cite web |title=Sheffield City Council Election Results 1973-2012 |url=https://www.electionscentre.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/Sheffield-1973-2012.pdf |website=Elections Centre |access-date=12 January 2026}} Labour regained the council in [[2004 Sheffield City Council election|2004]], but the Liberal Democrats formed their second majority administration in [[2008 Sheffield City Council election|2008]].{{cite news |title=Lib Dems take power in Sheffield |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/south_yorkshire/7378924.stm |access-date=12 January 2026 |date=2 May 2008}} Labour have been the largest party on the council since [[2011 Sheffield City Council election|2011]].{{cite news |title=Labour takes control of Sheffield City Council |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-south-yorkshire-13284970 |access-date=12 January 2026 |work=BBC News |date=5 May 2011}} However, following a loss of eight seats in [[2021 Sheffield City Council election|2021]], the party have been unable to form a majority administration. Labour initially formed a coalition with the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]];{{cite news |title=Sheffield City Council: Labour and Green coalition to run authority |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-south-yorkshire-57175934 |access-date=12 January 2026 |work=BBC News |date=19 May 2021}} from [[2022 Sheffield City Council election|2022]] onwards, though, both the Greens and the Liberal Democrats have joined with Labour to form a coalition.{{cite news |title=Labour, Greens and the Liberal Democrats agree collaborative way forward |url=https://sheffnews.com/news/labour-greens-and-the-liberal-democrats-agree-collaborative-way-forward |access-date=12 January 2026 |work=SheffNews |language=en |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220518184807/https://sheffnews.com/news/labour-greens-and-the-liberal-democrats-agree-collaborative-way-forward |archive-date=18 May 2022}}{{cite web |title=Three parties to lead Sheffield City Council for third year |url=https://www.sheffield.gov.uk/news/2025/three-parties-lead-sheffield-city-council-third-year |website=Sheffield City Council |access-date=12 January 2026}} In 2023, eight ex-Labour councillors formed an independent group, known as the Sheffield Community Councillors Group, thus forming the principal opposition on the council.{{cite news |title=Sheffield local elections: Fighting on locals’ behalf – what to expect from the Community Councillors Group? |url=https://www.thestar.co.uk/news/politics/sheffield-local-elections-fighting-on-locals-behalf-what-to-expect-from-the-community-councillors-group-4595809 |access-date=12 January 2026 |work=The Star |date=18 April 2024 |language=en}} Four councillors remain a part of this group. The seats up for election this year were last contested in 2022. In that election, Labour won 15 seats (down 1), the Liberal Democrats won 9 seats (steady), and the Greens won 4 seats (up 1).{{cite news |title=Sheffield result - Local Elections 2022
